Get one email when your Codex or Claude limit comes back.

ResetWatch is a small program that runs on your computer. It checks your usage every minute without sending any prompts, notes when a used-up limit resets, and emails you at that time.

Install Read the source on GitHub

Version 0.1.0. Free under the MIT License. Built from source on Windows, macOS or Linux.

The email you get

From
ResetWatch <onboarding@resend.dev>
Subject
Your Claude 5-hour limit is back. Get back to work

Rendered by ResetWatch’s own email code, with example values. Yours names your limit and uses your time zone.

1

How it works

  1. Every minute, it reads the same usage numbers that Codex and Claude Code show you. It sends no prompts, so checking uses none of your limits.
  2. When a limit reaches 100%, it saves the reset time to disk. The reminder survives a restart.
  3. At the reset time, it reads your usage once more and sends one email.

The email says one of two things:

“is back”
A fresh reading, taken after the reset, shows the limit below 100%.
“should be back”
It could not get a fresh reading, for example because you were offline or signed out, or another limit is still at 100%. Check before you start.

A limit that never reaches 100% never sends email. Each limit counts on its own: Codex and Claude, 5-hour and weekly.

2

Install

You need:

  • Git, and Go 1.27.2 or newer.
  • Codex signed in with a ChatGPT plan, Claude Code signed in with a Pro or Max plan, or both.
  • A free Resend account and API key. Resend delivers the email.

There are no prebuilt downloads and no hosted service. You build it and run it yourself.

  1. Build

    Open PowerShell in the folder that should hold ResetWatch.

    git clone https://github.com/ph03iA/resetwatch.git
cd resetwatch
go build ./cmd/resetwatch
.\resetwatch.exe version

  2. Set up

    Choose Codex, Claude or both, then enter your email. It asks for your Resend key without showing it and saves it to .env in this folder.

    .\resetwatch.exe setup

  3. Start watching

    Run it from the same folder and leave the window open. Ctrl+C stops it safely.

    .\resetwatch.exe watch

Which sender to use

Press Enter to keep the default sender, onboarding@resend.dev. It can only send to the email address you used to sign up for Resend. To send anywhere else, verify your own domain in Resend and use an address on it.

If Windows blocks it

Smart App Control can block a resetwatch.exe you built yourself, with the message “An Application Control policy has blocked this file”. ResetWatch cannot work around this.

After a restart

The watcher does not start by itself. Run watch again and saved reminders continue.

3

Commands

You need the first two. Run setup again to change your email or which tools are watched.

CommandWhat it does
setupGuided setup.
watchChecks usage every minute and sends due emails. Keep it running.
statusShows your last readings. Add --refresh to read fresh usage first.
historyLists reminder emails: sent, waiting or failed.
test-emailSends one email marked TEST, to check delivery.
versionPrints the version.

4

Limits

Read these before you rely on it. The exact rules are in docs/details.md.

  • Claude’s usage check is experimental. It uses the request behind Claude Code’s /usage screen. A Claude Code update may change it. If that happens, Claude emails say “should be back” and keep coming.
  • Your computer must be on. It has to be awake and online with the watcher running. Nothing runs in the cloud.
  • “Sent” means Resend accepted the email. Whether it reaches your inbox is up to your mail provider.
  • One account per tool. Two Codex workspaces on the same email address look the same.
  • Plans only. API-key, Bedrock and Vertex accounts have no plan limits to watch.

5

Privacy

This website

Collects nothing. It sets no cookies and has no analytics, forms or third-party scripts. Its fonts are served from this site.

The program

  • Keeps your settings, usage readings and email history in a local SQLite file on your computer.
  • Never reads your Codex or Claude credentials. It runs Claude Code with your hooks, plugins and MCP servers turned off.
  • Sends your email address and the email text to Resend over HTTPS, using your own Resend key. The key stays in .env or your environment and is never written to the database.

To report a security problem, see the security policy.
